topic: Geometric Interpretation of Non-Square Matrices: Dimensional Portals
target_audience: University students (Linear Algebra) or advanced High School students

sections.title: The Dimensional Portal Concept
lecture_lines: Square matrices transform space within the same dimension.
Non-square matrices act as portals between different worlds.
Meet Pixel, a cat living in a 2D grid.
animations: Create a 2D grid (#444444) with a small yellow circle labeled 'Pixel' (#FFD700) at position (1, 1).
Transform the 2D grid using a 2x2 rotation matrix; the grid rotates, but Pixel remains within the 2D plane.
Replace the grid with a glowing rectangular frame (#00FFFF) that pulses, representing a dimensional portal.

sections.title: Prerequisite: Basis Vectors as a Map
lecture_lines: Every matrix transformation is defined by its columns.
Columns show where unit basis vectors land.
These landing spots create the map for our space.
animations: Display a 2x2 matrix on screen with its two columns highlighted in red (#FF0000) and green (#00FF00).
Animate i-hat (#FF0000) and j-hat (#00FF00) moving from their basis positions to new coordinates (2,1) and (1,2).
The background 2D grid (#444444) warps and stretches to align with the new positions of the basis vectors.

sections.title: Tall Matrices: Upgrading Dimensions (2D to 3D)
lecture_lines: A three-by-two matrix takes two-D inputs to three-D.
We are upgrading from a flat plane to volume.
The original plane becomes a slanted sheet in space.
Pixel now exists on a tilted three-D surface.
His height depends on his original two-D position.
animations: Show a 3x2 matrix with 3 rows and 2 columns in white (#FFFFFF) centered on the screen.
Transition from a flat 2D grid to a 3D perspective view, introducing a third axis (#888888).
Draw two vectors representing the matrix columns in 3D space, then shade the plane (#00FF00, 0.3 opacity) they span.
Place the Pixel the Cat circle (#FFD700) onto the tilted 3D plane at a specific coordinate.
Animate a vertical dashed line (#FFFFFF) from Pixel to the XY plane to highlight his new Z-height.

sections.title: Wide Matrices: Downgrading Dimensions (3D to 2D)
lecture_lines: A two-by-three matrix squishes three-D into two-D.
This acts like a flashlight casting a shadow.
Imagine a three-D bird flying in the sky.
The matrix projects its shadow onto the ground.
Information is lost as volume collapses into area.
animations: Display a 3D wireframe cube (#0000FF) hovering above a flat 2D plane (#FFFFFF) representing the output space.
Project vertical 'shadow' lines from each vertex of the 3D cube down to the 2D plane.
Fade out the 3D cube, leaving only its 2D shadow projection (#444444) on the plane below.

sections.title: The Golden Rule: Row x Column Logic
lecture_lines: In an M-by-N matrix, N is the input dimension.
The number of rows, M, is the output dimension.
Columns dictate how many starting directions we have.
A one-by-three matrix sucks three-D space into one-D.
An entire room collapses into a single infinite line.
animations: Display text 'M x N' where 'N' points to a 3D volume [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/room.svg] and 'M' points to a 2D area.
Show a 1x3 matrix and highlight each of its three columns, linking them to X, Y, and Z directions.
Animate a 3D cloud of points (#FFFFFF) being sucked into and collapsing onto a single 1D line (#FF00FF).

sections.title: Summary: The Column Space Perspective
lecture_lines: Matrices transform vectors into a destination subspace.
This is just moving between different coordinate systems.
Dimensions are portals to new geometric worlds.
animations: Show two vectors (#FF0000, #00FF00) in 3D space with a shaded region indicating the subspace they span.
Morph a 2D coordinate pair into its corresponding 3D position on the span of the portal's columns.
